## Micron Faces Taiwan Strike Threat From Nearly 10,000 Workers

A strike at this scale in Micron's Taiwan operations could disrupt HBM supply at a moment of tight AI-driven memory demand; the confluence of this threat with tariff warnings to Korean memory makers creates a multi-front supply-side risk across the HBM complex — relevant for AI infrastructure cost and lead-time models.

- Approximately 10,000 Micron workers in Taiwan are threatening a strike, raising potential supply disruption risk at a material manufacturing site.
- The threat directly implicates Micron's Taiwan operations, which are relevant to HBM and NAND production capacity.
- No timeline, specific demands, or probability assessment is provided in the single-outlet headline.
- Read alongside the Samsung/SK Hynix tariff warning, the HBM memory supply chain faces simultaneous geopolitical and labor pressures.
